title: Roasted Butternut Squash Soup
subtitle: Creamy British soup with ginger and coconut
excerpt: Butternut squash roasted with a whole head of garlic until caramelised, then blended with coconut milk, ginger, and a little cumin. The roasting step is what gives this soup its depth.
sourceNotes: Butternut squash soup became a British cafe staple from the 1990s onward. Adding coconut milk and ginger brings a Southeast Asian warmth to an otherwise straightforward roasted vegetable soup.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze before adding coconut milk. Add when reheating.
recipe.batchNotes: Good for batch cooking. Scales up easily.

content.text: Leave the squash in the oven until it is very soft and browning at the edges. Undercooked squash gives a starchy, less sweet result.

items.prepNote: top sliced off to expose the cloves

content.text: Put the squash halves cut-side up in a large roasting tin. Add the onion quarters and the garlic head.
Drizzle everything with olive oil. Season well with salt.
Roast for 45 to 50 minutes until the squash is very soft and caramelised at the edges.
Leave to cool for 10 minutes. Scoop the flesh from the squash skin.
Squeeze the garlic cloves out of their skins.
Put the squash flesh, garlic, onion, and ginger in a blender.
Add the stock, coconut milk, cumin, and chilli flakes.
Blend until very smooth. Work in batches if needed.
Pour into a saucepan and heat through. Taste and adjust the seasoning.

items.symptom: Soup tastes starchy and not very sweet.
items.cause: The squash was not roasted long enough to caramelise.
items.fix: Return to the oven for another 10 to 15 minutes until very soft and browning.

items.symptom: Soup is too thick after blending.
items.cause: Less stock was needed once the squash was very soft.
items.fix: Add more hot stock or water a little at a time until the consistency is right.
